364214.ordinary: Literal read. Primary bodies read: arXiv:2408.01513 full-text extraction (Definitions 2.3-2.5, Conjecture 2.1, Definition 3.1 cover relation) and arXiv:1702.00866 full text (Conjecture 6.7, Prop. 3.3 rank = number of off-diagonal entries, Prop. 3.5/Cor. 3.6 Boolean-lattice base, Theorem 4.9 = Armstrong chi(P(1^n);q)=(q-1)^{C(n,2)}, Hallam-Sagan quotient Lemmas 2.4/4.4/4.6/4.8 and Prop. 4.7, Prop. 6.6, Conjecture 6.7 with computational verification to n=5). My own structural analysis: the recursion builds P(1^n) as a quotient of P(1,0,...,0) x B_{n-1} x ... x B_1 by classes {(A,S): A+S=X}; a class has size at most 2^{r-1} at the step adding hook sum position n-r+1, so the naive bound is prod 2^{r-1}=2^{C(n,2)}, and the n! bound is exactly a cancellation estimate at each of the n-1 quotient steps. Source's printed n=3 values (Example 3.2/Figure 5) give mu in {-1,-1,-1,2,1,-1} with max 2 <= 6, consistent with chi=(q-1)^3 and with the conjecture.
364214.prior: O'Neill 2018 poses Conjecture 6.7 and reports computational verification to n=5; the 2024 source lists it as open. Search 002 (query 2) located only the primary paper and mirrors, no proof, no counterexample, no later resolution. historical-results-allowlist.json has no entry for 364214, 1702.00866 or 2408.01513; inherited-denials.json has no matching blocked key.
364214.novelty: No public proof or refutation located within the bounded search. This is a bounded nonmatch, not a worldwide novelty claim.
364214.significance: A proof answers Pak's Question 1.4 (T(1^n)=e^{Theta(n^2)}) through T(1^n) >= 2^{C(n,2)}/n!, the only route the source proposes; a refutation kills that route and shows the source's computational evidence does not extrapolate.
364214.formal: Lean endpoint: for n : Nat, A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Nat with nonnegative entries and hook sums h_k = 1 for all k, |mobius 0hat A| <= n.factorial, where the order is the merge order with covers (i<j<k): a_ij+1, a_jk+1, a_ik-1 and (i<j): a_ij+1, a_jj+1, a_ii-1. Requires a Finset of matrices, a locally finite order instance on the subtype, the incidence-algebra Mobius function, and Int absolute value; no Tesler poset exists in Mathlib.
364214.independent: Independent adversarial check would have to re-derive the Hallam-Sagan quotient, verify the cover direction and rank, and audit any claimed cancellation estimate. Nothing is accepted here.
364214.acceptance: NO CREDIT. Deep route parked with a precise gap: the n! bound is a per-step cancellation estimate in the Hallam-Sagan quotient; the source supplies only the trivial 2^{C(n,2)} bound and no bound on class sizes.

360918.ordinary: Literal read. Primary body read: arXiv:2311.16665 abstract, Conjectures 2-3 (Bowler-Brown-Fenner), Theorem 4 (tree recognition for n>=5000), Section 6 Theorem 7 (5n/6+2 cards determine bipartiteness), and the explicit infinite families attaining floor(n/2)+1 common cards (Family 1 and Family 3 with n = 1 mod 4, and the diamond family of Figure 6). Independent structural reading: every card of a bipartite graph is bipartite, so a common card forces H-w bipartite, i.e. w lies on every odd cycle of H; the count of such w can be as large as n (H an odd cycle), so the bound must come from the G-side isomorphism-class count, which the source does not control below 5n/6.

source.name: Anthony B. Evans, Adam Mammoliti and Ian Wanless, Latin squares with maximal partial transversals of many lengths, arXiv:1911.05912 (2021); J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 180:105403 (2021), DOI 10.1016/j.jcta.2021.105403

344498.ordinary: Literal read. Primary body read in full-text extraction: Conjecture 4.1, Examples 4.1-4.2 (sharpness of alpha=1/2 and beta=2/3), Theorem 4.1 (Ryser embedding into some Latin square of order m), Theorem 4.2 (Kneser), Theorem 4.3 (abelian case), Theorem 4.4 (Olson), Theorem 4.5 (alpha/2+beta>1 case), Lemma 5.1 (subsquares are cosets of a subgroup). My own derivations: (1) row/column translation normalises 1 in X and 1 in Y, so X,Y are subsets of Z=XY and 1 is in Z; (2) D:=X^{-1}X = YY^{-1}, because for x1,x2 in X the b-subsets x1Y,x2Y of Z meet (2b>m) and symmetrically for Y; (3) X,Y are subsets of D; (4) if XZ=Z then Z is a union of left cosets of <X>, and |X|>m/2 forces a single left coset, whence |<X>|=m and Z is also a right coset (K g K subset gK forces g to normalise K), giving the conclusion; symmetrically ZY=Z gives H=<Y>; (5) therefore the only hard case has XZ!=Z and ZY!=Z, and Olson forces |X|+2|Y| <= 2m and 2|X|+|Y| <= 2m, i.e. m/2<|X|<2m/3 and 2m/3<|Y|<m with |X| <= 2(m-|Y|); (6) if either the left or the right stabiliser of Z has order m the conclusion holds, so in the hard case both have order at most m/2; (7) structural exclusions of the smallest hard sizes: in A_4 the normal V_4 forces |XY| to be a multiple of 4 when X lies in one V_4-coset and at least 8 otherwise, so m=7,a=4,b=5 is impossible; in D_8 the normal <r> forces |XY| in {4,8}; in D_22 the prime-order rotation subgroup plus Cauchy-Davenport forces |XY|>=11 for every split with |X|=6,|Y|=7; in S_3 and D_10 the same coset arithmetic gives no |XY|=7. No counterexample found.
344498.prior: Source proves the abelian case (Theorem 4.3) and the alpha/2+beta>1 case (Theorem 4.5) and explicitly leaves the nonabelian gap open. Search 002 (query 1) found no resolution; the 2026 Hilton/subsquare-free Latin square paper located is unrelated. Allowlist/denials: no match for 344498 or 1911.05912.
344498.novelty: The hard region is not covered by any located publication. The two structural lemmas above are elementary and would likely be judged routine by experts; no proof or counterexample is claimed.
344498.significance: A full proof settles a printed JCTA conjecture; a counterexample in the hard region refutes it. Neither is achieved, so the significance is potential only.
344498.formal: Lean endpoint: for a group G, Finsets X Y : Finset G and m : Nat with (X*Y).card = m, 2*X.card > m and 3*Y.card > 2*m, produce a subgroup H with H.toFinset.card = m, a left coset g • H.toFinset containing X and a right coset H.toFinset * {h} containing Y. Requires Finset products, Subgroup, cosets, and invariance of the conclusion under row/column translation.
344498.independent: Would need an independent check of the D-equality, the stabiliser dichotomy, and the claim that the hard region is nonempty.
344498.acceptance: NO CREDIT. Deep route parked with a precise gap: need a nonabelian Kneser-type theorem in m/2<|X|<2m/3, 2m/3<|Y|<m, |X|+2|Y|<=2m, 2|X|+|Y|<=2m; Olson's 1/2 bound is sharp there and yields no contradiction.
